doc.title: Orrin Evans interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Being a black man first and navigating the world
summary: Anecdote from Germany about being stared at in an Eagles jersey, and his view that he is a black man before a jazz musician.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now we can deal with it. You know? I got on the elevator the other day, someone said to me, we were in Germany and they said, “Man, do you ever feel weird.” And I was like, “Why?” They said, “Because I just swear all these people, every time they’re walking by they’re looking at you and do you ever feel weird that they’re just looking at you because you’re black?” And the Eagles had just won the Super Bowl so I came back and I had this big Eagles shirt on and a sweat suit that looked like I was from a reject Run-DMC movie. So I said, “I think they’re looking at me because I have this Eagles jersey and this reject sweat suit on.” And he laughed. But the point is I don’t even, you know, I don’t see that. And in that same conversation he was like, “How is it to be the only black person, you know, here?” I never really, now I consciously look, I’m like wait, I’ve been the only black person for the last four hours and I’ve seen a bunch of people. You know? But I guess my whole point of even bringing that up is this is the world I live in and I don’t plan on moving to a different world so I’m trying to figure out the best way to navigate my time here you know, and navigate my time where I enjoy every moment of it. And the biggest part of me is the fact that I’m not a jazz musician, it’s that I’m a black man. So I embrace that and I walk in this world just like everyone else. You know? I walk in this world just like everyone else. And once we all start to really embrace that I honestly think this will be a better world. You know? We can’t get through a lot of, you know, even driving here, honestly, there was about a good thirty mile stretch where I was like Lord if my car breaks down I’m not going anywhere near any of these houses and seeing anyone. So they’re out there. They’re out there. But we’ve got to — we have to be aware and stop honestly giving everybody their 15 seconds, 16 seconds of fame, and just really deal with the problem. That was a whole bunch of shit but hopefully it made sense.
